v.reasons: The claimed criterion, implemented from its mathematical statement (d_u = coefficients of p(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau r-periodic residue sums of p(q)(1-q), E_u = d_u - tau_u, K = D+1-r(b+1), u ranging over floor(K/2)+1..D+1-r, d_v=0 for v<0), matches the independently computed ground truth on all 37,790,700 claimed instances and on 6.42 million additional out-of-range instances (r up to 12, k up to 10, a_i up to 25, b up to 100), with zero mismatches; two independent implementations (C and sympy) agree. Caveat for the orchestrator: the criterion is correct but is a disguised form of the direct test. Anti-palindromy of p(q)(1-q) gives E_u = d_{D+1-r-u} (verified numerically on all 44M instances, identity_fail=0), so 'E_u >= d_{K-u}' is exactly 'c_v - c_{v-1} = d_v - d_{v-rb} >= 0 for 0<=v<(N+1)/2', i.e. first-half monotonicity of the symmetric coefficient sequence. The 'r | some a_i' disjunct is redundant (cond_true == unimodal count in every run). So Theorem A is a true iff-statement but not a closed-form parameter characterization in the spirit of the paper's floor-sum condition. Files: /tmp/claude-0/qu/review/r1/N_exact-B/check.c, xcheck.py, full_run.log, new_r7to10.log, new_bigA.log, new_random.log.
